bihar_raw_news.title: Tejashwi Yadav Flags Bihar Fiscal Deficit, Rising Debt | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: August 21, 2026 Bihar's Fiscal Deficit Touches 5.8%, Tejashwi Yadav Raises Alarm Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Bishnu J Tejashwi Yadav | Image Source: PTI Bihar Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav on Friday, August 21, raised questions over the state's finances, pointing to the rise in public debt and a fiscal deficit of 5.8 per cent of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) in 2025-26. In a social media post, the RJD leader said the numbers were worrying and accused the BJP-led NDA government of mishandling the state's finances. Yadav claimed the financial strain was being felt in government payments, alleging delays in payments to employees and pensioners, social security beneficiaries and contractors. He also said it was affecting spending on development work. He further claimed that allocations under the Student Credit Card scheme had been cut and that scholarships were being reduced. Yadav said Bihar's revenue deficit and debt had both increased and questioned the government's plans to improve revenue collection and keep the fiscal deficit under control. He also alleged that the state had taken on a large amount of additional debt over the past two years even as its finances remained under pressure. Calling the situation a "serious financial crisis", Yadav accused the NDA government of corruption and financial mismanagement. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar govt clarifies: No cut in student credit card Rs 4 lakh loan limit - EducationTimes.com
bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar government on Friday clarified that students would be able continue availing education loans of up to Rs 4 lakh under the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme. The Bihar State Education Finance Corporation will provide up to Rs 2 lakh, the statement said, while scheduled commercial banks will continue providing the remaining Rs 2 lakh to Rs 4 lakh. As per prior rules, the corporation itself provided loans of up to Rs 4 lakh. The statement came a day after Jan Suraaj functionaries, at a press conference, alleged that the Student Credit Card scheme had been diluted and the maximum loan amount reduced from Rs 4 lakh to Rs 2 lakh. According to a department release, Rajiv Raushan, secretary, higher education, said the change was aimed at expanding the scope of financial assistance for higher education. The scheme has also been linked with the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana, PM Vidyalaxmi portal and banks. Students, meanwhile, can avail education loans of up to Rs 10 lakh through PM Vidyalaxmi. The department said expenditure approval for the scheme had risen from Rs 886 crore in 2025-26 to Rs 950 crore in 2026-27, marking an uptick of Rs 64 crore. It said the figures showed financial assistance had not been reduced but expanded.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Gets 11.19 Lakh Pucca Houses with ₹13,427 Crore Allocation - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Gets 11.19 Lakh Pucca Houses with ₹13,427 Crore Allocation 21 Aug 2026 2 min read Why in News? Union Agriculture and Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced the approval of 11,18,937 pucca houses for poor families in Bihar , along with an allocation of ₹13,427 crore , during a State-level Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana programme in Patna on 20 August 2026 . Key Points: Housing Approval: A total of 11,18,937 pucca houses have been approved for poor families in Bihar. Financial Allocation: The approved housing package involves an allocation of ₹13,427 crore . PM Awas Yojana: The housing initiative aims to provide poor families with secure and dignified living conditions through pucca houses. Two-Year Progress: During the last two years, 24,30,327 houses have been approved for Bihar, involving a total expenditure of ₹29,164 crore . Crop Insurance: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) will now be implemented in Bihar to provide farmers protection against crop losses caused by natural calamities . Risks Covered: Crop insurance will provide protection against risks such as floods, drought, excessive rainfall and other natural calamities , subject to the scheme’s provisions. Women’s Empowerment: The government will focus on creating more Lakhpati Didis through Self-Help Groups, self-employment and group-based enterprises. She-Marts: She-Marts are proposed to be established in every district to provide Jeevika Didis and women’s Self-Help Groups with markets for their products. Rural Connectivity: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was highlighted as an important component of rural development by improving connectivity between villages, markets and essential services. Three Pillars of Rural Development: The government highlighted roads, houses and agriculture as three important pillars for improving rural livelihoods and strengthening the rural economy. national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Regional News 109 HM Amit Shah holds meeting with Gorkha leaders in Sukna
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah held an important meeting with senior Gorkha leaders today at a resort in Sukna, Siliguri. Chief Secretary Manoj Agarwal, Interlocutor Pankaj Singh, IB Director Mahesh Dikshit, Hill Affairs State Minister Bishal Lama, Lok Sabha MP Raju Bista, Rajya Sabha MP Harsh Vardhan Shringla, Gorkha Janmukti Morcha President Bimal Gurung, and Gorkha National Liberation Front President Mann Ghisingh were present. Five other Gorkha MLAs and some other Gorkha leaders were also present. Briefing the media after the meeting, Darjeeling Lok Sabha MP Raju Bista said that the meeting was very fruitful and that all the Gorkha leaders constructively presented their issues. After hearing the leaders, the Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari, also expressed his views and commitment regarding the concerned issues. After the meeting, the Home Minister announced that a high-level committee to resolve the issues would be formed under the chairmanship of Interlocutor Pankaj Singh, former BSF Director and Deputy National Security Advisor. GJMM Secretary Roshan Giri also briefed the media, stating that the meeting was very fruitful and satisfactory. Additionally, Harsh Vardhan Shringla emphasised that a solution for the Darjeeling Hills, Terai and Dooars regions should be achieved within the constitutional framework, a point on which all leaders agreed.

national_raw_news.title: BRICS delegates visit historic Thotlakonda Buddhist site ahead of Youth Ministers’ Meeting 5 hours ago 70
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, along with ministers and senior delegates from the BRICS countries, visited the historic Thotlakonda Buddhist heritage site near Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh. The delegates visited the ancient Buddhist remains, including the Mahastupa, meditation centres, wells and kitchen areas. They were briefed on the historical importance of the site and the life of Buddhist monks who lived there centuries ago. Dr Mandaviya also planted a sapling at Thotlakonda as part of the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign. The Union Minister appreciated the rich Buddhist heritage of Thotlakonda and said that India’s Buddhist heritage is important to the entire world. The visit is part of the programmes being held in Visakhapatnam under India’s BRICS Presidency 2026. Ministers and senior representatives from 11 BRICS countries are participating. The BRICS Youth Ministers’ Meeting will be held in Visakhapatnam this evening. The meeting, chaired by Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, will discuss ways to strengthen cooperation in youth development and empowerment, with a focus on education, skill development, entrepreneurship, wellbeing and sustainable development. The BRICS Sports Ministers’ Meeting will be held in Visakhapatnam tomorrow, with discussions expected to focus on strengthening cooperation in sports. The engagements provide an important platform to exchange national experiences, identify areas for practical cooperation and strengthen collective efforts towards youth participation, sports development and inclusive growth.
